profile.reading: This record is named Switch: The Rock in this registry, mapped to Williamson County, Texas, near Georgetown and Round Rock. The operator own Austin area page names this same facility The Rock directly, located at Dell Technologies global headquarters, with up to 1.5 million square feet of data center space, up to 2 MW per cabinet, 100 percent renewable energy, and a 100 percent power uptime guarantee. The page also notes the operator acquired Data Foundry locations in Austin and Houston in 2021 to anchor a fifth PRIME campus expansion in the Texas market.

reading.body:
Switch: The Rock is a 1.5 million square foot campus in Williamson County near Dell Technologies' Austin headquarters. The operator publishes cabinet density as up to 2 MW per cabinet, not a total facility power figure. If the entire space operates at typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack with two racks per cabinet, this would imply roughly 750 MW of potential IT load; the actual figure depends on tenant workloads and utilization, neither published here.

The campus is certified for 100 percent renewable energy and 100 percent power uptime. The operator acquired this site as part of a fifth PRIME campus expansion in Texas in 2021. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, only 18 of which publish power figures; this campus does not appear among the 18 published figures in the state registry, placing it outside the top tier of disclosed capacity in Texas.

The absence of a published total MW figure limits what can be concluded about this campus's role in AI scaling. The scale of available space and the renewable certification suggest it is positioned to host large workloads if tenants arrive, but the grid constraint on AI scaling cannot be assessed without knowing actual power allocation to the site.
